name: Auction Draw Dominoes
description: Auction Draw Dominoes is a high-stakes gambling variant of the classic Draw Dominoes game. It introduces a chip-based economy where players pay to draw tiles from the boneyard, and most uniquely, participate in a competitive auction for the final two remaining tiles in the boneyard. The winner of the hand claims the entire accumulated chip pool.
origin: Modern gambling variant of Draw dominoes played with chips and an auction for the last tiles, described in English-language domino circles.

history.origins: A derivative of the standard 'Draw' domino game, adding elements of poker-style betting and auction theory. Likely developed in tavern settings where gambling on dominoes was a common pastime, and documented in English domino circles.
timeline: Unknown: Traditional Draw dominoes establishes the core matching mechanic.
1900s: Gambling variants like Auction emerge, adding chip pools to social games.
Present: Popular in regions where dominoes remains a primary social competition.
history.cultural: Used as a 'session game' where players can drop in and out of the pool between rounds.
history.evolution: The transition from score-based winning to pool-based winning allows for shorter, more intense rounds.

setup.players: 2-4 players. Each starts with an equal stack of chips.
setup.dealing: 2-3 players: 7 tiles each. 4 players: 6 tiles each. Remaining tiles form the 'Boneyard'.

rules.objective: Be the first to 'Domino' (play all tiles) to win the chip pool. If the game is blocked, the player with the lowest total pips wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Matching**: On your turn, you must match one end of a tile in your hand to an open end on the board. 2. **Drawing**: If you cannot play, you must draw tiles from the boneyard one at a time. For each tile drawn, you must pay 1 chip into the pool. 3. **The Auction**: When the boneyard is reduced to exactly **two tiles**, play freezes. An auction begins for those two tiles. 4. **Bidding**: Every player has a chance to bid twice (or check) in clockwise order. The highest bidder takes BOTH tiles into their hand and adds their bid to the pool. 5. **Ending**: A player wins by playing their last tile. If no one can play and the boneyard is empty, the game is 'Blocked'.
keyRules: Bid Limit: You cannot bid more chips than you currently possess.
Blocked Win: In a blocked game, the player with the lowest pip total on their remaining tiles wins the pool.
No Passing: You MUST play if you can. You MUST draw if you can't play and tiles are available.

strategy.basic: Keep track of which numbers are 'open'. Avoid being the one who has to draw and pay chips into the pool.
strategy.intermediate: The Auction Decision: Bid for the last two tiles if your hand is nearly complete and needs 'flexibility' (new numbers), or if you want to prevent an opponent from potentially winning.
strategy.advanced: Value of Information: In the auction, if you hold most of the remaining 5s and 6s, and the board has open 5s and 6s, the auction tiles are less valuable to you because you already control those paths.
tips: Don't overbid in the auction unless you are 80% sure you will Domino. Losing the auction AND the hand is a double loss.
Save your doubles for late-game play if they match the board ends.

variations.name: Heavy Ante
variations.description: Players contribute a larger initial amount, making the auction bid relatively less significant.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes how many chips players ante at the start; the core phases and engine settings stay the same.

scoring.description: Winner takes the entire pool accrued from the ante, the draw payments, and the auction bid.
scoring.winCondition: Emptying your hand first or holding the lowest pips in a block.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience Draw Dominoes with a cutthroat gambling twist. Manage your chips as you draw from the boneyard, then compete in the final high-stakes auction for the last remaining tiles. Empty your hand and sweep the pool.
